rigid_flow — 3D scene_flow3d op

• Data kinds: points × points → pose

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.rigid_flow(pts0, pts1, max_iter: 'int' = 20) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import scene_flow3d; scene_flow3d.rigid_flow(pts0, pts1, max_iter: 'int' = 20) -> 'dict'; from the registry, ops3d.get("rigid_flow"))

• Return value through the ledger: fullseye.ledger.rigid_flow(...) returns only the declared out type pose (the underlying function also returns auxiliary values). When you need what was dropped, use fullseye.ledger.rigid_flow.raw(...) or call scene_flow3d.rigid_flow directly.

Usage

Estimate the single rigid motion that explains pts0 -> pts1, via nearest-neighbour correspondences and Kabsch (ICP-like).

Starting from the identity transform, at each iteration takes nearest-neighbour correspondences from the point cloud at the current pose to pts1, solves (R, t) in closed form with registration.kabsch, and accumulates. Stops when the correspondence indices match the previous iteration (= convergence) or at max_iter. The convergence test depends only on the stability of the indices, so it is scale-invariant (no absolute epsilon is used).

Args:

pts0: (N, 3) point cloud at time 0 (N >= 3, to determine the rotation uniquely).

pts1: (M, 3) point cloud at time 1 (M >= 1, need not match N).

max_iter: upper limit on ICP iterations.

Returns:

dict: {"R": (3,3) rotation, "t": (3,) translation, "rmse": point-to-nearest-neighbour RMS distance after alignment}. R is a true rotation (det=+1). rmse is the measured value (nothing faked).

Raises:

ValueError: invalid shape, pts0 < 3 points, or pts1 empty.
